2 months!

I’ve learned so much, made alot of GREAT memories, kept my grades up, met professors I genuinely love, and had WAY more random side quests than I ever expected.

But the best part has easily been the people. I’m so grateful for all the friends I’ve made, the late-night shenanigans, random plans, and all the little moments that make college feel like home.

And I’m just as excited for all the friends I haven’t met yet and the memories we still have to make.

Life is good. College is fun. And if this is only the first 2 months, I can’t wait to see what the next 4 years bring.

One of the hardest product shoots I’ve pulled off, but I’m really happy with how these turned out.

Shot for @twistedpendant , featuring their Italian 925 Silver Cuban Chain (5MM) and Italian 925 Silver Cuban Bracelet (5MM).

I really wanted to do this shoot right because jewelry is a market I’ve been wanting to break into, and I wanted to make a strong first impression. That meant spending sooo much extra time on the concept, lighting, motion, reflections, and the small details that make silver jewelry actually look good on camera. I have learned ALOT through this experience.

The original photos were taken by me using a subwoofer, water, and paper to create the effect practically in-camera. 

AI was used ONLY to enhance the Twisted Pendant logo and “925 ITALY” text so those details stayed clean and readable.

The pieces themselves are great. They feel solid, the finish looks clean, and the detailing gave me a lot to work with creatively.

Big thank you to @twistedpendant for sending these out and trusting me with the shoot.

https://twistedpendant.com

@kencarson — xperimenting tour

Set 4/4
Last Ken Carson post.

It was a pleasure having this opportunity, and I loved every minute of it. Easily the ultimate college sidequest.

I’m super happy with how some of these turned out (set 3/4 >) especially considering this was my first concert shoot.

Thank you to everyone who supports me and helps make opportunities like this possible. I genuinely appreciate it.

I know some of the last photos are pretty rough, but Ken’s set was VERY hard to capture. The lighting was constantly changing from fire to lasers and everything in between. I also wasn’t in the pit for the concert , so i had to avoid flying water bottles and an absolutely insane mosh pit.

Definitely learned a lot from this experience. I’d love to do more concert photography whenever it fits with my schedule.
